newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end near flat on local funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end near flat on local funds support.

text.p: Malaysian shares prices ended a rollercoaster Friday practically unchanged, with local funds supporting the market as foreign funds continued to be net sellers, local analysts and dealers said.
At the close, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks gained 0.64 to 1,041.91. The index had dived to 1,018.79 earlier, its lowest in 1997.
"Foreigners are still selling. We have had some large foreign sell orders, and there does not seem to be much sign of a recovery," said Ralph Dixon of the international division of T.A. Securities.
Local funds began buying blue-chip stocks in the afternoon session, after the government released better-than-expected economic data earlier, dealers said.

Malaysia's Consumer Price Index for April grew at 2.6 percent on a year-on-year basis, its lowest level for around six years, analysts said. In March, the country's trade balance posted a surplus of 1.75 billion ringgit.
Analysts said the trend may not last, as certain large import items are expected to crop up in future reports.
Volume jumped up to 290 million shares, valued at 1,770 million ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 503 to 151.

The day's most active stock was MBf Capital rising 42 cents to 4.26 on persistent rumours of a possible merger with Suria Capital. Suria gained 13 cents to 2.58 ringgit. Over 25.3 million shares of MBf Capital changed hands, while Suria's volume stood at 8.7 million shares.
Newly-listed Timberwell TWEL.KL ended its first day of trading at 7.30 ringgit after debuting at 6.50 on an offer price of 3.60 ringgit.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot May contract climbed 13.5 points to 1,028.5, June futures rose 12.0 to 1,031.0, and September futures gained six points to 1,047.0. Volume for May stood at 1,965. The June contract saw 27 lots changing hands, and September had 58 lots traded.
